description: AgMIP-Wheat collaborators released a high-yielding traits experiment for crop-model comparison. It covers 11 growing seasons at selected sites in Argentina, Mexico and Chile under well-watered, fertilised conditions. Two wheat genotypes are represented. The deposit includes daily weather, soils and starting conditions, cultivar traits, flowering and maturity dates, biomass, grain yield, yield components and intercepted radiation. Daily and final outputs for 25 crop variables from 29 models accompany the field measurements, with formatted analysis data and R code. Harvard Dataverse’s public dataset API confirmed the named version 2.1 release and CC0 1.0; DataCite lists RAR packages. No price was shown. A food-supply modeller can assess high-yield trait representation and compare model predictions with observations. These managed, high-yielding sites cannot establish performance under water or nutrient stress. The archive was not downloaded, so variable-level completeness remains unchecked. This resource is related to earlier AgMIP wheat datasets in G4-0566 and G4-0571, but its sites and experimental aims differ. The former water-sector rejection did not assess this crop-simulation use.
name: Data from the AgMIP-Wheat high-yielding traits experiment for modeling potential production of wheat: field experiments and multi-model simulations
